raw_response:
Aiya, let me think about this year. I'll talk it through first, then lay it out properly.

---

**My thinking:**

I'm 48, been working this land since I was a girl. My husband goes to the city for construction work most of the year — comes home at busy times like wheat harvest and cotton picking if I really need him. Kids are grown, working outside. So it's mostly just me on these 10 mu.

I keep about 7 mu in wheat-maize rotation — that's our grain, can't give that up. The other 3 mu or so I keep in cotton. I know, I know, a lot of the women my age have quit cotton because it's too much work. But I've grown cotton for thirty years, I know how to handle it, and the price was decent last year. My husband comes back to help with the picking. Same as last year, no reason to change.

**Wheat** — already in the ground since last October. I planted Jimai, the usual variety the station sells. At sowing I put down one bag of 15-15-15 compound for every two mu, that's my base. Right now the wheat is greening up, so I'll go out with urea soon — about half a bag per mu at green-up. Then I'll irrigate. Water from the well costs money so I watch it: once at green-up, once around jointing, and one more later if it doesn't rain. Spray once for weeds, that's usually enough. Last year I got about 400 kg per mu. If the spring isn't too dry I should get the same.

**Maize** — I plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June. No time to plow, the window is less than a week. The man in our village with the no-till seeder does the whole field for me, I pay him per mu. I buy Zhengdan 958 seed or whatever the shop has, hybrid, can't save maize seed. Apply compound with the seeder, then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage when it's knee-high. Usually one or two irrigations in July if the rains are late. Spray once for weeds. Last year I got about 450 kg per mu.

**Cotton** — plant late April. I plow and ridge the 3 mu in early April, put down a bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base — cotton is hungry. Lay plastic mulch film, plant by hand with the film. During the summer I topdress urea once around flowering. Spray many times — bollworm, aphids, the little whiteflies. That's what makes cotton expensive and a headache. Pick by hand starting September, three or four rounds through October. My husband comes back for picking, and I hire a neighbor woman for maybe ten days. Last year I got around 230 kg lint per mu, the price was okay.

I'm watching the budget. Fertilizer is expensive these days. I won't cut back on it though — without fertilizer the yield falls and I can't recover. The place I save is labor: I do most things myself, hire only when I must.
